primary_passage.author: Isidore of Seville
primary_passage.domain: Legal terminology within an encyclopedia; no herb or medical identification claimed
primary_passage.complete_paragraph_transcription: Precarium est dum prece creditor rogatus permittit debitorem in possessione fundi sibi obligati demorari, et ex eo fructus capere. Et dictum precarium quia prece aditur, quasi precadium, R pro D littera commutata.
primary_passage.transcription_status: Complete paragraph from online Latin transcription, not a diplomatic transcription of the1472 print. Modern punctuation and capitalization retained.
primary_passage.interpretation: The text explicitly names R replacing D. This is not merely an edit operation guessed from two similar words. Its folk-etymological account is not asserted to be correct linguistic history.

occurrence_roles.role: Defined legal headword in a denotational explanation. This is still a definition, not unambiguous ordinary narrative use.
Explicit hypothetical etymological operand, not asserted independently attested ordinary vocabulary

printed_primary_witness.inspection: PDF downloaded and page9 rendered and manually viewed; do not use noisy OCR as exact printed letters.
visually_observed_variants: Print reads prece additur, while selected online transcription reads prece aditur.

The operand at the end of the line appears as precadiu with final-m abbreviation or omission; it is not visibly a fully spelled precadium. The presence and exact extent of its abbreviation bar need a separate close diplomatic reading.
The following line visibly names r pro d littera commutata.
printed_primary_witness.no_silent_expansion: precadiu[m] is an editorial expansion convention, not a claim that all nine expanded letters are nine printed glyphs. Full online paragraph and printed evidence remain separate.

other_transmitted_reading.observed_search_excerpt: Et dictum precarium, quia prece additur, quasi prece adium, r pro d littera commutata.
other_transmitted_reading.inspection_level: Indexed primary-text excerpt, not independently checked page image; not adopted as a second exact experiment text.
other_transmitted_reading.consequence: prece adium cannot silently be collapsed into precadium: spacing and the extra e affect the literal string relation. Do not pool editorial/transmitted versions.

source_only_literal_checks.warning: Patterns are separately canonically relabeled strings; the actual common-letter alignment is precad-ium versus precar-ium. No Voynich spelling or symbol value assigned.

candidate_and_rival.candidate: A single shared spelling channel for complete ordinary prose, quoted operands and letter mentions. Under a fixed injective letterwise channel, replacing encodedD by encodedR at the specified position must turn encodedprecadium into encodedprecarium; the encodedR must also equal position2. The defined headword and later mention must share their lexical spelling under a declared case convention.
candidate_and_rival.rival: An ordinary lexical codebook plus a separate quotation/letter channel can preserve the stated semantic explanation while allowing the ordinary headword representation to differ from its quoted spelling. A loose etymological paraphrase likewise need not preserve the exact literal operand relation.
candidate_and_rival.discriminating_consequence: Only a separately fixed complete writer and source-to-target alignment makes the cross-channel equality predictive. Finding a pair of one-edit native forms alone cannot choose the candidate over the rival.
candidate_and_rival.scope_limit: This paragraph provides explicit operation, operands, letter names and a repeated defined headword. It does NOT yet provide a clearly nonmetalinguistic use of that word in a separate ordinary sentence or episode. The strongest IDEA1050 use-versus-mention binding is therefore incomplete.

access_and_review.bounded_source_search: Primary Isidore texts; herb chapter17 did not supply a verified explicit named-letter edit in the bounded search. Grammar examples1.35 supply edits but not clearly separate ordinary use. Candidate5.25.17 retained without forcing an herbal match.

decision: Retain complete primary passage and unresolved spelling/use-mention limits as source evidence. Do not select a native mapping, quote-only hit, lexical meaning or full writer from this source-only result.
